boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on streets and corridors within Gettysburg College’s practical off-campus orbit, each paired with one sourced reason to go.

cards.title: Settle In at Gettysburg Library
cards.subtitle: Baltimore Street — public reading and study space
cards.notes: Walk south on Baltimore Street for a public study stop; check the branch page before going because daily closing times vary.
cards.short_summary: A downtown library branch with evening hours on several weekdays.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gettysburg Library is at 140 Baltimore Street and lists branch hours through 8:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Sunday 1–5 p.m.; Monday–Thursday 9 a.m.–8:30 p.m.; Friday–Saturday 9 a.m.–5 p.m. Confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Catch a Film or Performance
cards.subtitle: Carlisle Street — cinema and performing arts
cards.notes: Check the current calendar, then walk Carlisle Street to the box office; buy only through the theater’s official channels.
cards.short_summary: Gettysburg College’s downtown venue presents films, performances, and community events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Majestic Theater is located at 25 Carlisle Street and sells tickets for cinema and live events through its website and box office.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists box-office hours and says the box office closes 30 minutes after the performance or final movie begins.

cards.title: See Lincoln’s Arrival Point
cards.subtitle: Carlisle Street — preserved 1859 railroad station
cards.notes: Continue along Carlisle Street to examine the historic depot; consult the seasonal schedule before planning an interior visit.
cards.short_summary: A preserved downtown station associated with Lincoln’s 1863 arrival in Gettysburg.
cards.evidence_claim: The station at 35 Carlisle Street opened in 1859 and is identified as the place where Abraham Lincoln arrived on November 18, 1863.
cards.source_title: Gettysburg Lincoln Railroad Station™ | Destination Gettysburg
cards.access_notes: The published schedule is seasonal, with limited operating days outside the May-to-Labor-Day period; verify before entering.

cards.title: Browse a Free Artifact Collection
cards.subtitle: Baltimore Street — privately operated history museum
cards.notes: Follow Baltimore Street to the museum and call ahead for current hours; viewing the collection does not require admission purchase.
cards.short_summary: A free private museum displaying thousands of historical artifacts.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gettysburg Museum of History at 219 Baltimore Street identifies itself as a free museum with more than 4,000 artifacts.
cards.access_notes: The museum instructs visitors to call for current hours.

cards.title: Trace a Civilian Family’s Wartime Story
cards.subtitle: Baltimore Street — restored Civil War-era home
cards.notes: Reserve a guided visit before walking down Baltimore Street; allow time for the artifacts and preserved evidence uncovered during restoration.
cards.short_summary: A restored home interpreting the Battle of Gettysburg through the Shriver family.
cards.evidence_claim: The Shriver House Museum at 307 Baltimore Street offers guided tours about the Shriver family and displays original artifacts and preserved bullet holes.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists Saturday and Sunday hours of 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and recommends reservations; verify the schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Start with an Orientation Film
cards.subtitle: Steinwehr Avenue — museum and battlefield orientation stop
cards.notes: Use Steinwehr Avenue for a museum introduction before exploring farther; confirm current admission options and program times online.
cards.short_summary: An orientation center combining exhibits, short films, visitor services, and a bookstore.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gettysburg Heritage Center at 297 Steinwehr Avenue offers a museum, orientation film, licensed battlefield guides, special events, and a bookstore.
cards.access_notes: Check the official visit page for current operating information and ticket requirements before departing.

cards.title: Study the Battle’s First Day
cards.subtitle: Seminary Ridge — museum inside a battle-era building
cards.notes: Head west to Seminary Ridge for exhibits on the first day, the building’s hospital use, and the national conflicts surrounding the war.
cards.short_summary: A museum interpreting battle, medicine, and moral choices inside historic Schmucker Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum at 111 Seminary Ridge interprets Gettysburg’s first day of fighting, a major battlefield hospital, and dilemmas that divided the nation.
cards.access_notes: The official site currently lists daily hours of 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; verify hours and admission before visiting.

cards.title: Take the One-Mile Walking Path
cards.subtitle: Long Lane — 52-acre public recreation park
cards.notes: Follow Long Lane to the park for a paved one-mile walk or the fitness trail; check posted rules before using courts, fields, or the skate park.
cards.short_summary: A large municipal recreation space with walking, fitness, play, and sports facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The 52-acre park at 545 Long Lane includes a mile-long paved walking path, a 20-station fitness trail, courts, playgrounds, fields, and a skate park.
cards.access_notes: Facility rentals and organized programs require separate arrangements; observe on-site rules and posted availability.

cards.title: Meet Local Growers on Saturday
cards.subtitle: Long Lane — seasonal open-air market
cards.notes: Time the Long Lane trip for Saturday morning during market season; browse local produce and goods without assuming every vendor accepts the same payment.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal nonprofit market connecting shoppers with Adams County agriculture.
cards.evidence_claim: The Adams County Farmers Market operates at Gettysburg Recreation Park, 545 Long Lane, seasonally on Saturdays from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m.
cards.source_title: Adams County Farmers Market | Destination Gettysburg
cards.access_notes: The destination page lists seasonal Saturday hours of 8 a.m.–1 p.m.; verify current market dates before going.

cards.title: Pause Among the Local Art
cards.subtitle: Chambersburg Street — coffeehouse and gallery space
cards.notes: Walk west on Chambersburg Street for coffee, food, and the displayed artwork; use the garden or porch when conditions permit.
cards.short_summary: A downtown coffeehouse combining a food menu with indoor art and outdoor seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Ragged Edge Coffeehouse at 110 Chambersburg Street serves coffee, smoothies, breakfast and lunch items and provides an art gallery, garden, and front porch.
cards.source_title: Ragged Edge Coffeehouse and Catering | Destination Gettysburg
cards.access_notes: The destination page lists 6:30 a.m.–6 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and 6:30 a.m.–9 p.m. Friday–Saturday; confirm before visiting.
